tagline: Two miles to a port town that sold for $4.25.
intro: Orton Road leaves NC 133 just south of Wilmington, and Plantation Road and St. Philips Road carry the byway a little over two miles toward the Cape Fear River. Shortly before the byway begins, drivers cross Allen Creek, once Lilliput Creek, after a plantation granted in 1725 and named for the imaginary country in Gulliver's Travels. Near Orton Plantation alligators sometimes sun themselves beside the road. It ends at the entrance to Brunswick Town.

Brunswick was a busy colonial port and home to two royal governors. British raiders burned most of it in 1776, only a few families came back after the war, and by 1830 the empty town site was sold to the owner of Orton Plantation for $4.25.

moments.title: Orton Plantation
moments.text: Union troops used the house as a military hospital after Fort Fisher fell, which spared it, and since a 2010 sale the grounds have been closed to the general public.

moments.title: St. Philip's Church
moments.text: Paid for partly by selling goods and enslaved people taken from an abandoned Spanish privateer ship in 1748, the roofless church still shows where Union cannonballs struck its walls in 1865.

moments.title: Fort Anderson
moments.text: In 1862 Confederate engineers heaped earthworks over the burned colonial town to guard Wilmington, sparing only the church, and the garrison pulled out in 1865 after a Union attack.
